name: apple

attributes.attribute: the most magical fruit to the Celts, a talisman of good fortune and prosperity

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The apple is a symbolic fruit. It is the most magical fruit to the Celts. It appears in many myths and legends. It hides in the word Avalon, the Arthurian Otherworld. It is the fruit on which Connla of the Golden Hair was fed by his fairy lover. The soul of king Cú Roí rested in an apple within the stomach of a salmon. It was one of the goals of the fated Sons of Tuireann. In the Cotswolds of Britain, an apple tree in blossom out of season meant coming death. The apple stood for harmony and immortality, abundance and love. It was a talisman of good fortune and prosperity. Some scholars connect the word to Apollo. His name may have been Apellon, drawn from the same source as the word apple.

okr.objective: Record the apple as a symbolic fruit.
